Red Roses, Green Gold is an entertaining reimagining of the nostalgic and transportive music of the Grateful Dead, in a new theatrical context and style.
The versatile musical talents of the performers, who go effortlessly from one instrument to another while singing full-out in vivacious arrangements by Jeff Chimenti, are simply jaw-dropping.
There are wonderful songs...The music is admirably performed...and a storyline so poorly conceived and executed that it almost ruins the fun.
In short, you might have a perfectly good time at “Red Roses, Green Gold,” even if it’s less a diamond in the rough and more fool’s gold.

cn.t: Critics find this Grateful Dead jukebox musical features strong performances and beloved songs, but suffers from a weak, clunky plot that undermines the show's appeal even for devoted Deadheads.
